title: UserSWE: Evaluating Coding Agents in Multi-Turn Conversations with Dynamic Users
abstract: arXiv:2610.29822v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As coding agents become more capable, developers increasingly use them to fix bugs through multi-turn interactions. Existing benchmarks do not adequately cover this scenario. Most present a complete issue report in a single turn without interaction. Their evaluation can produce both false positives and false negatives, accepting incorrect patches or rejecting correct ones. We introduce UserSWE for evaluating coding agents' ability to fix repository-level bugs through multi-turn interactions with dynamic users and execution-grounded verdicts at every turn. Its construction pipeline turns repository history and existing single-turn benchmarks into multi-turn tasks. At each turn, information pools constrain what the simulated user can reveal, while a persona chain sampled from a transition model calibrated on 20,859 development sessions governs how it speaks. translated_title: UserSWE：在与动态用户的多轮对话中评估编码智能体
translated_abstract: 随着编码智能体能力的不断提升，开发者越来越多地通过多轮交互使用它们来修复漏洞。然而现有基准测试未能充分覆盖这一场景：大多数基准在单轮中一次性给出完整的问题报告，缺乏交互过程。这类评估可能同时产生假阳性和假阴性结果，即接受错误的补丁或拒绝正确的补丁。我们提出 UserSWE，用于评估编码智能体通过与动态用户进行多轮交互来修复仓库级漏洞的能力，并在每一轮对话中都提供基于执行结果的判定。其构建流程将仓库历史和现有单轮基准转化为多轮任务。在每一轮中，信息池约束模拟用户可以透露的内容，而由基于 20,859 个开发会话校准的转移模型采样得到的人格链则控制模拟用户的说话方式。每一轮结束后都会运行测试，并由来自不同模型家族的一对智能体（原文摘要在此处被截断）……
tldr: 提出 UserSWE 基准，通过动态用户多轮交互与每轮基于执行的判定，评估编码智能体修复仓库级漏洞的能力。
en_tdlr: UserSWE is a benchmark that evaluates coding agents on fixing repository-level bugs through multi-turn interactions with dynamic users, featuring execution-grounded verdicts at every turn.
